newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares rise on stronger dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares rise on stronger dollar.

text.p: Swedish shares rose on a firmer dollar on Tuesday as several blue chips have large U.S. sales.
The general index rose 0.34 percent to a record high of 2,385.38 in turnover of 4.26 billion crowns.
Among sectors, the forestry group was the winner, up 1.31 percent in relief as pulp prices seem to be on their way up rather than down, dealers said.

Non-traded forestry group Sodra and listed Stora both announced that they will attempt to see through price rises on long-fibre pulp to $610 a tonne from $560 in February, after failing to lift prices on January 1.
Stora rose two crowns to 95.5, while MoDo advanced 2.5 to 199, SCA gained three to 142.5 crowns and AssiDomaen edged 0.5 higher to 187.5 crowns.

Forestry sector shares also benefited from the stronger dollar and so did automotive group Volvo, which rose two crowns to 152.5 crowns. But truck maker Scania slipped 0.5 to 166.5 crowns on a newspaper article forecasting a weaker truck market.
Engineering group ABB rose 15 crowns to 789 after confirming its negotiating about an order in India.
